allow.title: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
allow.reason: No patched release exists — the advisory covers <=2.0.2 and 2.0.2 is the newest published version. It reaches us only through pptxgenjs@4.0.1 (the latest, which pins image-size ^1.2.1), so there is no version of either package that resolves it. npm's suggested fix downgrades pptxgenjs three majors to 1.1.5, which would break PPTX export outright.
allow.reachability: NOT REACHABLE — and NOT because of our call sites. Re-verified 2026-09-05, correcting the original rationale, which said image-size runs whenever pptxgenjs measures an embedded image via addImage(). That was wrong: pptxgenjs@4.0.1 declares image-size but never loads it AT ALL. The string 'image-size' appears in neither shipped entry point (dist/pptxgen.cjs.js, dist/pptxgen.es.js) nor their sourcemaps, so it is absent from upstream's own TypeScript source. The only sizing call site, getSizeFromImage, ships inside a block comment marked 'FIXME: TODO: currently unused', and even that dead code requires 'sizeof' — a different package that is not installed. The bundles' only literal requires are 'jszip' and that commented 'sizeof'; their only dynamic imports are node:fs and node:https; there is no createRequire, eval or Function constructor able to build a require at runtime. Runtime proof: after require('pptxgenjs') plus a full write() of a text+table deck AND a deck calling addImage() with both a data URI and a filesystem path, require.cache held zero image-size entries. That our sole consumer (src/app-layer/reports/risk-report-render.ts) calls only addText/addTable is a second, independent reason — but this exemption no longer rests on it.
allow.upgradePlan: Watch for an image-size release >2.0.2 or a pptxgenjs release that drops the dependency, then delete this entry — the gate fails if it is stale. Note the tripwire is NOT 'someone added addImage()'. That was the original condition and it is not the real risk: addImage() does not load image-size either. The real risk is pptxgenjs — declared ^4.0.1, so a minor bump installs with no code change here — shipping a version that wires the dependency up for real. The npm-audit gate cannot see that: it re-checks whether the ADVISORY still applies, never whether this REACHABILITY claim still holds, so it would stay green while this justification silently became false. tests/unit/pptx-image-size-unreachable.test.ts fails in exactly that case (mutation-proved). If it goes red, this exemption is void until re-argued.
allow.doNotOverride: Do NOT add an `overrides` entry forcing image-size 2.x. It is futile AND breaking. Futile because 2.0.2 is itself in the advisory range (see `reason`). Breaking because v2 changed the module's public shape — measured 2026-09-02 on a clean install of image-size@2.0.2: `typeof require('image-size')` is `object`, not `function`, with keys [default, disableTypes, imageSize, types]. v1 exported a callable directly, so any consumer doing `require('image-size')(buf)` gets a TypeError. package.json also moves `main` from dist/index.js to ./dist/index.cjs and gains an `exports` map. Worst of all, the failure would surface only on the first PPTX export that embeds an image — a path nothing exercises today — so the break would ship silently and stay hidden.

allow.title: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
allow.reason: Same package, same absence of a fixed release (<=2.0.2 vulnerable, 2.0.2 is latest) and the same pptxgenjs pin. Listed separately so a partial upstream fix — one advisory patched, the other not — cannot be masked by a single entry.
allow.reachability: NOT REACHABLE. Identical mechanism to GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr: the JXL/HEIF parsers cannot be entered because pptxgenjs@4.0.1 never loads image-size on any path — the dependency is declared in its package.json but referenced nowhere in its shipped bundles, and its one sizing call site is commented-out dead code that names a different package. Not contingent on our call sites; addImage() does not load it either. See the sibling entry for the full runtime proof.
allow.upgradePlan: As above — both entries should disappear together when image-size ships a fix; if only one does, the gate starts failing on the other, which is intended. The shared reachability basis is guarded by tests/unit/pptx-image-size-unreachable.test.ts; if that test goes red, BOTH entries are void.
